decision.question: What is Panel2's drawer breakpoint, and how does a side become a drawer?
options: reuse ext/drawer (the site's global right-rail singleton)
a small CSS transform at grip.css's own 34em floor
decision.why: ext/drawer is one global, app-wide rail wired to the site's own ☰ and url state (?drawer=ai) — it does not fit in one import for an arbitrary per-panel side, and the brief says build a second drawer system only if ext/drawer doesn't fit in one import. 34em is grip.css's own existing floor for "a rail stops being a rail", reused rather than invented.

decision.question: How does Panel2.split resize two panels?
options: a third static part, Panel2.Split, holding both children
a plain static function returning a div, reusing ext/grip exactly as Sidebar/drawer already do
decision.why: the 'parts as statics' rule is for pieces of ONE panel's own chrome a caller might subclass (Header/Side); the split wrapper has no content or state of its own to subclass. Written up in doc/decisions.md in case a real need to promote it ever shows up.

decision.question: How should several Panel2s arrange themselves on a dashboard (the owner's 'I forget how that works' question)?
options: a new grid formula in panel2.css
reuse framework.css's existing .grid.auto formula (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(var(--column),100%),1fr))) with panel2's own default --column
decision.why: framework.css already ships the exact formula the brief describes; CLAUDE.md law 6 (one of everything) and the css skill (write as little new CSS as possible) both argue against a second copy of the same formula.

decision.question: How to prove the phone-width drawer live instead of only a screenshot?
options: a static screenshot (explicitly allowed by the brief for the phone case)
a real narrow <iframe> reloading this same demo page, guarded by ?view=phone to avoid infinite recursion and to keep the embedded render small
decision.why: an iframe gets its own real viewport, so the @media (width < 34em) rule fires for real — not a simulation the demo stage's zoom-based width presets can't trigger for a viewport media query. Verified live with a headless Playwright probe: the closed side's transform (translateX(-256.688px)) changes to none after clicking the toggle, zero console errors.
